en.body: But, best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be rajasic when it is performed for reward or for show. The word dambhartha, for display, is what exposes the ego. A sacrifice done to be seen is classified as rajasic, driven by restlessness and a desire for reward. Krishna then names the third kind of sacrifice, one that is performed without faith, rule, or care.

issues: contrast_template: "जो यज्ञ सिर्फ दिखावे के लिए किया जाए, वह यज्ञ नहीं, बल्कि सत्ता का दावा है।" (The notice uses 'बल्कि' (but/rather) to create a contrast, implying that a sacrifice done for display is 'not a sacrifice at all but a claim to power'. The original source and its fixed English translation simply classify it as a 'rajasic' sacrifice; it does not state that it is 'not a sacrifice' or a 'claim to power'.)
unsupported: "सत्ता का दावा है।" (The claim that a showy sacrifice is a 'claim to power' is an unsupported interpretive addition not found in the source verse or the standard Mahabharata narrative.)
